answer: Seal each bond's signing key in a hardware root, so one machine can back one identity at a time. Split release across three independent auditors, each holding a share and checking a different log. Catch duplicates by replaying the work transcript, not by comparing names. A thousand clones then need a thousand distinct roots and three cooperating auditors each. That is the measured price, and it turns the nebula of cheap names into a dune of failed replays once the opal of a clean record is required to unlock.
